brief: Apple has been largely untouched by the recent tech-market selloff, diverging not only from the semiconductor index (SOX), which the note says is unsurprising, but now also from the rest of the Magnificent 7, a divergence the note calls remarkable. AAPL trades near all-time highs, closing in on NVDA as the world's most valuable company. The note frames Apple as tech's defensive play: its forward FCF yield of about 3.15% sits above the Nasdaq 100's (NDX), and Apple's rolling two-month correlation with the NDX has turned negative for the first time on record, which the note reads as a flight to safety within tech. The note also revives a September 23 thesis that Apple is an unintended beneficiary of the AI trade. Since that note, AAPL has outperformed NVDA, and the six-month performance gap between the two has widened further. Apple's implied volatility has risen as investors buy protection, but that stress is described as modest next to the broader surge of fear across tech.
